sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

title.narrative: # training centers equipped with new tools

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of RAC training centers that will be upgraded with modern, service-specific tools and equipment procured through the project. “New tools” refers to toolkits and training sets that enable practical, hands-on training in the safe handling of HFC alternatives, leak detection, recovery and recycling, and energy-efficient servicing practices.

This indicator measures the number of formal monitoring visits carried out by the project team (UNDP/NOC) to training centers and servicing workshops equipped under the project. The purpose of these visits is to verify equipment installation and use, assess compliance with safeguards (including gender and disability inclusion), and gather feedback from beneficiaries.

title.narrative: # workshops equipped with equipment and toolkits

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the number of RAC servicing workshops that have received and installed new servicing equipment and toolkits procured under the project. Toolkits include recovery machines, leak detectors, vacuum pumps, and other specialized instruments required for the safe handling of HFC alternatives and the application of good servicing practices.
